reviews.notes: Clayed empty earth, first man already arrived safely beside elder creator, and compact clay/footprint symbol. Descent output was blocked and replaced by a DIFFERENT later narrative moment; no full human in selected huella. Flat layered material, muted palette; spatial continuity illustrative, not identical physical sets.

Younger female Sun and older male Moon distinct; solar ages represented by former horizons and three arcs, current Sun distinct. Symbolic heads do not claim authentic iconography; paper-cut with air and muted palette.

Raw food on sun-warmed stone before local fire; distant opposing-bank hearth; Mamu spits one ember after river crossing and remains a toad. Third piece is compact toad/ember/river assemblage, no humans, no quilling. Food and house geometry remain editorial reconstructions.

Two adult men at doorway, small cotton-seed handoff, complementary cut-paper palms and cotton boll in symbolic closing. No treaty, massacre, universal peace or imported Aruaco insignia. Visitor garment and dwelling are generic artistic reconstructions, not documented Aruaco dress.

Older sick father, wife and two departing adult sons; later healthy festive apparition in wind before sons. Feather crown/achiote/thread attire restricted to this explicitly described narrative, NOT community uniform. Symbolic gap across macana is an editorial distancing device, not literal broken weapon or endorsement of matricide. No killing pictured.

Three adult travelers reach a round burial-linked house, two warn the third; later a natural jaguar and two fleeing survivors, no attack or corpse. Closing is compact house/jaguar ambiguity, not monster or authenticated witch symbol. No claim that every jaguar is a returning witch; no invented cure or destruction ritual.
Three cane arrows from rainbow bow and three trajectories/routes; extra sun removed, exactly one ordinary sky sun. Compact three-arrow/path closing; no modern city founding, map or dates.

Milling-stone memory and restrained separated adult confrontation; symbol stone rebuilt as visibly flat stacked grey cardstock. Other-group appearance deliberately generic, not authenticated Aruaco costume; no celebration of violence or colonial-savior image.

Totumo flood island with anonymous non-diagnostic karau and Nuti; flooded surface above underground multilevel refuge now visible. Closing intentionally combines OWL transformation, totumo, Nuti and flood/fire traces across different phases; it does NOT show karau taxonomy or claim these all share one literal instant. No ark, drowned bodies or graphic harm.

Day and midnight collective ceiba cutting, maize cob visible in both crowns; unintended gourd fruits removed. Symbol is pale CEIBA-WOOD cut rings and one flat-kernel maize cob, not a deep earth/water aperture. One small moon is an editorial midnight cue.

Drought and small seed reserve, then communal planting ON moisture-holding fallen log rather than soil. Closing simplified to log/seeds/shoot; added bag and thin curled root strands removed, no quilling. No miraculous field or deity reward.

Exactly father and three adult sons; first failed pull then third son raises stick clear and water appears. Parent torso/son's stripe corrected for continuity. Closing has no human and is a symbolic stick/water association, NOT a literal temporal frame showing the extraction; do not use huella as action keyframe.

Entry corrected to ordinary forest house and lone traveler, no outdoor standing ghosts. Act has dead residents seated and answering in an incomprehensible language, not silence or pursuit. Doorway/negative-space and separated paper sound arcs are editorial boundary metaphor, not authentic signs.

Chicha gathering then two adult perpetrators alone on NIGHT path; straight-haired and curly-haired departing pair aligned. No victim body or consumption pictured. Flat club and empty third footprint closing expresses concealed absence, not an ethnic custom, confession or punishment; decorative cord removed.

Departure toward Gran Río and fatigued adult return, no second attack, dead children or medical rash. Elder's upper torso aligned; closing is two gender-neutral empty paper cut-outs and bows separated by river, an editorial paired-loss metaphor, NOT proof of cause or justice.

Natural tapir calling to share and monkeys answering in morning; extra upper sun removed, exactly one sky sun in act. Compact monkey communication symbol, broad flat sound arcs, no human clothes or animal council. Species remain anonymous/non-diagnostic, not zoological certification.

Hunter and monkey before impact, same recovered arrow; action reframed with whole hunter within canvas and spacious forest. Third shows one actual arrow plus opposite-direction dark paper arrow metaphor on leaf; not a second weapon or authentic glyph. Human death omitted graphically.

Sleeping dream is a separated paper inset, waking traveler now matches younger black-haired protagonist instead of elder. Tree begins to fall without impact; log/tapir shadow/human footprint closing is editorial inversion, not verified supernatural causality or injured body.

Two hunters encounter mythic BEFORE-shell creature in tree; this is not real zoology. Ending has bark-shell morrocoy alone by creek, all three unintended human spectators removed. No intermediate murders, cooking, Wuacha or Jacinto. Current shell symbolic bark-paper association, not precise species study.

Yunari body/territory and branching waterways, two current/future earth levels with opposite light. Closing now exactly FIVE EARTH slabs plus separate water/darkness underneath; fourth second from top supported by TWO pillars on third, fifth above. No full body in closing, no planets, labels or authenticated sacred diagram. Future people and thick-paper skin suggestion remain artistic, not ethnographic costume.

Yaau and Numirinta opposite complementary horizons, equal participation with exactly TWO maize cobs; people shown as abstract adult cutouts, not biological birth or Papá Grande clay/fall. Closing flattened to broad maize silhouettes and oval cardstock kernels, no rolled tubes/quilling. Footprints are editorial metaphor; frame left/right is not a surveyed East/West map.
